syllabus.clause: and boundedness as backpressure → Rust Systems Engineering Ch.7, Ch.10

items.item: struct holds unmasked, monotonically increasing in/out counters plus a mask
length is in minus out; empty is in == out; full is length greater than mask
fifo size must be a power of two

sources.source: Agner Fog, Optimizing software in C++

items.item: simple integer and bitwise operations cost about one clock cycle
integer division costs dozens of clock cycles, and a power-of-two division becomes a shift
a bounded deque discards from the opposite end once full, on every new item
a full bounded channel's send blocks until the buffer opens up
a ring buffer never grows: capacity is fixed at construction, unlike topic 1's doubling array
wrap-around via modulo is correct for any capacity, but only a power-of-two capacity lets a bitwise AND replace it
head equals tail is structurally ambiguous between empty and full under naive masked indices, since both states wrap identically
unmasked indices avoid the ambiguity because in and out keep counting forever and are only brought back into range at the moment of array access, so their difference is always the true occupancy

sacrificing one slot (capacity usable = allocated minus one) and keeping an explicit count or flag are both real, workable alternatives, each paying a different cost (wasted capacity; or an extra write on every push and pop)
overwrite and block are policy choices about what happens on a full write, independent of which full/empty mechanism is underneath

a bounded structure forces a producer to either lose old data (overwrite) or slow down to the consumer's pace (block) — an unbounded structure defers that choice by growing instead, which is exactly what backpressure refuses to do
the concurrent, lock-free version of this same structure is a materially harder problem (multiple threads racing on the same in/out counters) and is left entirely to the Rust chapters
masking vs modulo is measured directly in examples.py at several capacities rather than asserting the cited cycle counts transfer unchanged to the machine running the example
a correctness check (masked-index ring buffer vs a naive modulo version) agrees exactly across a long randomized sequence of pushes and pops, including ones that wrap the buffer multiple times
